Swedish Cardamom Buns

Served at: Second Sunday of Advent

Makes 12-16 bunsPrep 45 min (plus 2-3 hours rising time)Cook 12-15 min

These fragrant Swedish Cardamom Buns, known as kardemummabullar, are a beloved treat, especially during the Advent season. Their warm, spicy aroma fills the home, creating a cozy atmosphere perfect for reflection and anticipation as families gather to light the second candle of Advent. Enjoy them with a cup of coffee or tea as a delightful fika tradition.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, melted, plus 1/2 cup (113 g) softened for filling
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons (1 packet) active dry yeast
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom (for dough), plus 1 tablespoon (for filling)
  • 1 large egg (for dough), plus 1 large egg, beaten (for egg wash)
  • 4 to 4 1/2 cups (480-540 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) light brown sugar, packed
  • 2 tablespoons pearl sugar (optional)

Method

  1. Warm the milk in a small saucepan or microwave until it reaches about 105-115°F (40-46°C). Pour into a large mixing bowl.
  2. Stir in the melted butter, granulated sugar, salt, yeast, and 1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom into the warm milk. Let sit for 5 minutes until foamy.
  3. Whisk in one large egg. Gradually add 3 cups (360 g) of flour, mixing until just combined.
  4. Add the remaining flour, 1/2 cup (60 g) at a time, mixing until a soft dough forms. It should be slightly sticky but pull away from the sides of the bowl.
  5. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  6. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let rise in a warm place for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, or until doubled in size.
  7. While the dough rises, prepare the filling: In a small bowl, cream together the softened butter, brown sugar, and 1 tablespoon ground cardamom until well combined.
  8. Once the dough has doubled, gently punch it down. Turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and roll it into a large rectangle, approximately 12x18 inches (30x45 cm).
  9. Spread the cardamom filling evenly over the entire surface of the dough.
  10. Fold the dough in half lengthwise, creating a 6x18 inch (15x45 cm) rectangle.
  11. Using a sharp knife or pizza cutter, cut the dough into 12-16 strips, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) wide.
  12. Take one strip, twist it several times, then wrap it around two fingers to form a knot, tucking the end underneath. Alternatively, you can simply coil it into a spiral.
  13. Place the shaped buns on baking sheets lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between them.
  14. Cover the buns loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let them rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
  15. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
  16. Brush the risen buns with the beaten egg wash and sprinkle with pearl sugar, if using.
  17. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.
  18. Transfer the buns to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • For an extra cardamom kick, lightly crush whole cardamom pods and use the freshly ground seeds instead of pre-ground.
  • If you don't have pearl sugar, a simple glaze made from powdered sugar and a touch of milk or water can be drizzled over the cooled buns.
  • These buns are best enjoyed fresh, but can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or frozen for longer storage.
